tonight.headline: Pickens gave you 28.0 and a 27-point start; Tate's back was a tweak in Thursday's practice
body: Bad news first. You are 0–4 and last in a waiver order that never resets. Carnell Tate's back injury now has a cause and it is a fresh one: he tweaked it in individual drills on Thursday and went to the head trainer. Barkley has not practised all week and Philadelphia's beat writers expect him to sit.

The good news is real. George Pickens caught 9 of 13 targets for 130 yards and a touchdown last night, 28.0 in your flex, and your opponent's Cowboys defence scored 1. You lead 28–1, ESPN projects 133.6 to 110.1 and gives you 63%. Your lineup is still the projection lineup. The one thing left is Sunday 09:30: if Tate is inactive, Golden.

case.label: Last night
case.body: Tampa Bay 24, Dallas 16. Dallas trailed and Dak Prescott threw 42 times. CeeDee Lamb had 2 catches on 5 targets before his quadriceps tightened and he left with 6:14 to play (ESPN's Todd Archer via ClutchPoints; Athlon, 9 Oct); Buccaneers.com says corner Zyon McCollum had him covered before that. Pickens's 13 targets are a season high (archive: 6, 8, 11, 3, 13).

case.label: Their side
case.body: Nacua 21.7, Goff 18.5, Kyren Williams 17.9, Jeremiyah Love 15.1 (limited Wednesday and Thursday; his coach says the ankle should not affect Sunday), Watson 13.8, Kittle 13.7. The Cowboys' defence, projected 8.4, is banked at 1. Tee Higgins is still in their flex at 0.0 after missing a second practice, with Omarion Hampton, 11.6, on their bench: their 110.1 moves by about eleven when they fix it, and you cannot stop it.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Tate missing this afternoon's practice, on your side. On theirs, the flex fix. A 27-point lead on Friday is one receiver's game; eight of your nine have still to play.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Fallback only · both kick off Sun 11:00 Mexico City · read this afternoon's report · inactives 09:30
doFirst.title: If Tate is inactive: Golden
doFirst.subtitle: He tweaked his back in individual drills on Thursday and saw the head trainer. One practice left. Do nothing now; Golden plays at the same hour.

case.label: What happened
case.body: ESPN's Turron Davenport saw Tate 'tweak' his back during individual drills at Thursday's practice and then spend time with head trainer Matt Gregg (relayed by Draft Sharks, 9 Oct 00:37; I did not see Davenport's own post). The Titans listed him limited (titans.com, 8 Oct). So it is a new injury from Thursday, not something carried from the game. Houston's copy calling it a knee looks like a mix-up with Gunnar Helm, who is the knee.

case.label: How serious
case.body: Unknown. He finished the session as a limited participant, which is better than leaving it. Heavy's writer expects him to play if the week goes well; that is an opinion. No Titans coach has spoken about it. ESPN added a questionable tag and left his projection at 13.6, so none of this is priced.

case.label: The fallback
case.body: Golden, 12.7, the lineup check's own answer: Green Bay's lead receiver, not on the injury report, kicking off at 11:00 like Tate, so the swap can wait for the inactive list at 09:30. He faces Chicago, fifth-stingiest to receivers; Tate faces Houston, who allow the most. That is why this is a fallback and not a swap: 0.9 apart, a coin flip that goes to the projection.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Tate is active and Golden outscores him on Sunday (archive): then the coin flip lost, and no thesis was written on it. If Tate is inactive this card fires.

whatWentWrong.title: Tate's back is a fresh tweak from Thursday's practice
whatWentWrong.lead: Hurt in individual drills, seen by the head trainer, limited for the rest. He is your second receiver against the defence that gives receivers the most.

case.label: The evidence
case.body: Davenport's observation, relayed by Draft Sharks at 00:37 on 9 Oct; titans.com's Thursday report: limited, back, not listed on Wednesday. No coach quote.

case.label: What it changes
case.body: The one card. He stays in the lineup with Golden named behind him. A back tweaked two days before a game is the kind of thing that can go either way on a Friday.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: A full practice this afternoon and no game status takes the card away. A missed practice makes Golden the likely starter, and the decision is still made at 09:30 on Sunday.

Nothing overnight names Pittman's replacement or puts him on injured reserve.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: Six targets in all four games, the one without Pittman included (archive). 10.3, below Golden on your bench, so he would not start. He is a free agent, which matters now that you are last in the waiver order.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Eight or more targets against Indianapolis on Sunday. Then he is a free add for Rice's or Barkley's seat only if one of them is ruled out for a stretch, because both are protected while a teammate is hurt.

worthALook.sources: Steelers Depot · The Fantasy Footballers · Week 1–4 archive · waiver_analysis.py

worthALook.name: Brenton Strange
worthALook.lead: You held him for three hours on Wednesday. Free again, level with Loveland, and not a move.

case.label: The role
case.body: 7 catches on 8 targets for 95 in Week 4 with every Jacksonville pass-catcher healthy (archive). Targets 3, 2, 5, 8. Not on Jacksonville's report all week.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: 9.7, the same as Loveland, and the seat changed twice on Wednesday. Philadelphia allow the fifth-fewest points to tight ends (FootballDB, PPR, re-read Fri 9 Oct) and Jacksonville are off in Week 7; Loveland has no bye until Week 10.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Loveland ruled out. Nothing else reopens the seat before 14 Oct.

worthALook.sources: Week 1–4 archive · Jaguars Wire · FootballDB · activity log

worthALook.name: T.J. Hockenson
worthALook.lead: The highest-projected free tight end. Jefferson and Addison both practised on Thursday, which takes targets back.

case.label: The role
case.body: 13 catches on 13 targets for 119 with Jefferson out (archive). Jefferson was limited on Wednesday and Thursday and aims to play; Addison was limited on Thursday (vikings.com, 8 Oct). No game statuses yet.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: 10.4 against Loveland's 9.7 is a coin flip, the seat is closed, and Minnesota are off in Week 6, which would empty the slot again in five days.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Loveland ruled out and Jefferson ruled out with him.

worthALook.sources: Week 1–4 archive · vikings.com · ESPN league file

worthALook.name: Will Shipley
worthALook.lead: The handcuff to your Barkley, who is trending out. No coach has said how he and Pierce share it.

case.label: The role
case.body: Barkley missed Wednesday and Thursday and PhillyVoice's Jimmy Kempski expects him not to play (via Heavy, 9 Oct 06:01 ET); Bigsby is on injured reserve. Outlets expect Shipley to start. ESPN projects him 10.2.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: Those are outlets' reads, with Dameon Pierce on the 53, Carson Steele a possible elevation and no coach quote. 15 carries all season (archive); his career highs are 10 carries and 34 yards (NBC Sports Philadelphia). 10.2 is below Tuten, Kamara and Gordon, and he would be running against your own defence.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Barkley going on injured reserve. Then the seat question is asked again, and the only unprotected seat is Golden's, who is not a drop for a handcuff.

worthALook.sources: philadelphiaeagles.com · Heavy citing PhillyVoice · NBC Sports Philadelphia · Week 1–4 archive

doNotChase.name: Jacoby Brissett
doNotChase.lead: The biggest riser on your wire this morning, on a matchup. He projects half a point under Lawrence.

case.label: The rise
case.body: Arizona are at home to Detroit, who have allowed the most points to quarterbacks through Week 4 (FootballDB, PPR). SportsGrid's waiver column picked him out for it on 6 Oct. He is not on Arizona's injury report and he is a free agent, so he would cost no priority.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: 17.6 against Lawrence's 18.1: the projection still prefers the quarterback you have, by a coin flip, and the strategy's most expensive mistake was switching quarterbacks on a hunch. His Week 4 line was 21 of 35 for 166 with two touchdowns and three interceptions (SportsGrid).

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Lawrence on a Jaguars injury report, or ESPN moving Brissett above him by two points or more.

doNotChase.sources: FootballDB · SportsGrid · azcardinals.com · ESPN league file

doNotChase.name: Mark Andrews
doNotChase.lead: His quarterback has not practised this week.

case.label: The rise
case.body: The steadiest targets of the free tight ends: 6, 7, 5, 6 (archive).

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: Lamar Jackson (ankle) did not practise on Wednesday or Thursday (baltimoreravens.com). Jesse Minter: 'There will be a point later in the week when we'll figure out where it's at'; Rapoport has him unlikely, and Tyler Huntley took the first-team work. Andrews himself (hand) practised in full. 9.6, level with Loveland, for a closed seat.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Jackson practising this afternoon, and Loveland ruled out.

doNotChase.name: Malik Washington
doNotChase.lead: Carried, nothing new: target share in an offence that ran 37 plays last week.

case.label: The rise
case.body: 5 catches on 5 targets for 67, 12.0 (archive). Not on Miami's report. Hafley on last week: 'The problem last game was we ran 37 plays' (DolphinsTalk, 8 Oct).

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: Targets 8, 5, 10, 5 (archive). He would be your sixth receiver.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Eight or more targets against Cincinnati, or a different quarterback in Miami.

doNotChase.name: Makai Lemon
doNotChase.lead: Three Eagles receivers are now hurt, which is a real reason. He has not passed six points in a game.

case.label: The rise
case.body: DeVonta Smith and Hollywood Brown did not practise on Wednesday or Thursday and Dontayvion Wicks hurt a hamstring in Thursday's session (philadelphiaeagles.com, 8 Oct 18:00). If all three sit, the receivers are Darius Cooper, Lemon, Britain Covey and Elijah Moore. No statuses yet.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: 3 catches on 6 targets for 27, 5.7, with Smith already out; 2.5, 1.9 and 5.9 before that (archive). And he would be catching passes against your own defence.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Eight or more targets in London.

doNotChase.name: Dontayvion Wicks
doNotChase.lead: Philadelphia's most-used receiver, and now hurt himself.

case.label: The rise
case.body: The lead receiver with Smith out, by Bleeding Green Nation's account.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: He hurt a hamstring during Thursday's practice and finished limited (philadelphiaeagles.com, 8 Oct). 5.2 and 4.8 in the last two weeks (archive).

case.label: What would change it
case.body: A full practice this afternoon and eight or more targets in London.

waiverAnalysis.summary: The same eight names clear the tool's bar as on Thursday, and at running back and receiver the bar is an artefact: it measures them against Barkley and Rice, whose last week was an injury exit each. Four weeks of data. Nothing overnight turned a role reason into a move, and you are last in the waiver order.

rising.name: Keaton Mitchell
rising.roleReason: A three-man rotation with Omarion Hampton and Kimani Vidal: 10 carries and 6 targets in Week 4 (archive). None of the three is on the Chargers' Wednesday or Thursday report (chargers.com). Off in Week 7.
rising.action: WATCH — a committee third; the trigger is Hampton missing a game

rising.name: Brian Robinson Jr.
rising.roleReason: Bijan Robinson is healthy and not on Atlanta's report (baltimoreravens.com's copy, 8 Oct). 14 carries for 62 last week behind him (archive); the 25.7 was touchdowns. Nothing found on his role this week.
rising.action: WATCH — touchdowns and game script behind a healthy starter

rising.name: MarShawn Lloyd
rising.roleReason: Not on Green Bay's Thursday report and listed as the starter in Bleacher Nation's preview (8 Oct); Chris Brooks (ankle) missed both practices. 7 carries for 13 in Week 4 (archive). Nothing new on Josh Jacobs, who is still on the exempt list as far as anything found says. You dropped Lloyd for Gordon.
rising.action: WATCH — volume at under two yards a carry in a backfield nobody has won

rising.name: Mike Washington Jr.
rising.roleReason: Ashton Jeanty's handcuff: 9 carries for 18 in Week 4 (archive). Jeanty went from a full practice on Wednesday to limited on Thursday with the ankle (patriots.com's copy of the Raiders' report, 8 Oct). Nothing on Washington himself.
rising.action: WATCH — a downgrade for Jeanty, not an absence; nothing unless he misses Friday

rising.name: Khalil Shakir
rising.roleReason: 7 catches on 8 targets in the game DJ Moore left with an aggravated AC joint (archive). Moore did not practise on Thursday, Buffalo's first session; Schefter does not consider it long-term (ClutchPoints; Heavy, 8–9 Oct).
rising.action: WATCH — depends on Moore sitting on Monday night

rising.name: Tyquan Thornton
rising.roleReason: Out 12 to 16 weeks after ankle surgery, as reported on 5 Oct and carried; nothing new was found. The tool still prints him because his last game was his biggest.
rising.action: WATCH — off the list: out until at least January

rising.name: Keon Coleman
rising.roleReason: 6 catches on 7 targets for 116 after DJ Moore left (archive). The role is exactly as long as Moore's absence; Moore missed Thursday's practice and his coach expects him to try to play on Monday.
rising.action: WATCH — a role that exists only while Moore is out

rising.name: Roman Wilson
rising.roleReason: Michael Pittman Jr. re-injured his foot and will miss 'multiple weeks' (McCarthy via Steelers Depot, 8 Oct); no replacement has been named. Wilson was the second receiver beside DK Metcalf when Pittman sat in Week 2, on 55 of 70 snaps, and drew the same six targets he draws every week (archive).
rising.action: WATCH — a real vacancy and, so far, a flat six targets; he is free, so waiting costs no priority
rising.sources: Steelers Depot · The Fantasy Footballers · Week 1–4 archive
